saints.name: The Presentation of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saints.title: Memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saints.shortBlurb: The memorial of Mary's dedication to God in the Temple as a young girl, all her life consecrated to the Lord…
biography: This memorial, kept on 21 November, honours the presentation of the child Mary in the Temple at Jerusalem. The canonical Gospels do not record the event; it comes from the Protoevangelium of James, an apocryphal writing which relates that at three years of age Mary was brought by her parents to the Temple in fulfillment of a vow, to be reared in the Lord's service.

The feast arose in the Christian East, probably in Syria, the home of those apocrypha; it stands in Byzantine liturgical books by the eleventh century and was a recognized festival under Manuel Comnenus in 1166. In the West it was introduced at Avignon by Philippe de Mazieres and celebrated before the cardinals in 1372, spreading thence to Paris and the German dioceses.

Sixtus IV received it into the Roman Breviary, Pius V struck it from the calendar, and Sixtus V restored it in 1585, and it has been kept in the Roman rite ever since. Its lesson is not a single scene but the truth the scene expresses: that Mary was wholly given to God from her earliest years, a living temple made ready for the coming of the Lord.
saints.knownFor: Mary's consecration to God from her childhood.

sources.text: Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), “Feast of the Presentation of Mary”
